Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 62, verse 1:

Surat al-Jumu'ah (Makkan? no: Madaniyyah, Medinan) and its verses are eleven.

Correction to the above: the heading reads "Madaniyyah" and the verse count is eleven, so the translation is:

Surat al-Jumu'ah [Madaniyyah, and its verses are eleven]

﴿Yusabbih Allah﴾ yunazzihuhu (He glorifies Allah, i.e., declares Him far above what is unfitting), so the lam (in Allah) is extra. ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ — mentioning "whatever" is a form of taghlib (giving precedence to the majority), for the majority [of what is in the heavens and earth is non-rational]. ﴿The Sovereign, the Holy﴾ — the One exempt from whatever is not befitting to Him. ﴿The Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ — in His dominion and His making.

He it is who raised among the unlettered (ummiyyin) a messenger from among themselves, the Arabs. The unlettered (ummi) is one who cannot write or read a book. [He is] a messenger from among them: he is Muhammad (ﷺ). Reciting to them His verses: the Qur'an. And purifying them: cleansing them from polytheism (shirk). And teaching them the Book: the Qur'an. And the wisdom: what it contains of rulings. And indeed (wa-in) is the light (mukhaffafah) form of the heavy (thaqilah) form, and its noun is omitted, meaning wa-innahum (indeed they): they were before that, before his coming, certainly in clear (mubin) error, evident.

﴿And others among them⦆ is coordinated with "the unlettered ones," meaning those who exist among them and those who come from them after them, ﴿who have not yet joined them⦆ in precedence and virtue. ﴿And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise⦆ in His dominion and His making. They are the Successors (al-Tabi'un), and restricting the reference to them is sufficient to explain the virtue of the Companions (al-Sahaba), among whom the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, over all others to whom he was sent and who believed in him from all of mankind and jinn until the Day of Resurrection, because every generation is better than the one that follows it.
﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills.﴾ (It refers to) the Prophet and those mentioned with him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 62, verse 5:

﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah﴾ were charged with acting upon it, ﴿then they did not carry it﴾ they did not act by what is in it concerning his description (ﷺ), so they did not believe in him, ﴿is like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾ i.e., books, in that it gains nothing from them. ﴿Wretched is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah﴾ which confirm the Prophet (ﷺ), and the object of the dispraise is omitted, its estimated sense being "this likeness." ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 62, verse 6:

﴿Say, "O you who have Judaized, if you claim that you are allies of Allah, to the exclusion of [other] people, then wish for death, if you are truthful."﴾ The two conditions are connected to "fa-tamannaw" (then wish for), with the first being a restriction on the second; that is, "if you are truthful in your claim that you are allies of Allah." The ally (wali) prefers the Hereafter, and its beginning is death, so wish for it.

And they will never wish for death, because of what their hands have sent forth. [This is] from their disbelief in the Prophet, which necessitates their lying. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers, the disbelievers.

Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed," ﴿Say: Indeed, the death from which you flee - then indeed it will meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ The *fa'* (الفاء) here is *zā'idah* (superfluous, i.e. an extra particle that adds no meaning to the sentence). ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ means the secret and the manifest. ﴿He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ means He will recompense you for it.

O you who have believed, when the call is proclaimed for the prayer on the day of Friday (jumu'ah), [the preposition] "min" being in the sense of "fi" (in), then proceed (fas'aw, "hasten" in the sense of "hurry on" to) the remembrance of Allah, meaning the prayer, and leave off trade (wadharu al-bay'), meaning abandon its contract. That is better for you, if you know that it is better, so do it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 62, verse 10:

﴿Then when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾ an command of permission; ﴿and seek﴾ i.e., seek ﴿of the bounty of Allah﴾, the provision; ﴿and remember Allah much﴾ remembrance, ﴿that you may be successful﴾ i.e., that you may prosper. He (ﷺ) was delivering the Friday sermon when a caravan arrived, and a drum was beaten for its arrival, as was the custom, so the people left the mosque to go out to it, except for twelve men, and then this (verse) was revealed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 62, verse 11:

﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it﴾, i.e., the trade, because it is what they seek, rather than the diversion; ﴿and they leave you standing﴾ during the sermon. ﴿Say: What is with Allah﴾ of reward ﴿is better﴾ for those who believe ﴿than diversion and than trade. And Allah is the best of providers﴾. It is said: every person provides for his dependents, i.e., from the provision of Allah the Exalted.
